title: Matched-range fits showed higher total phosphorus at fixed sediment and flow at two Gulf outlets in 1981-1996 and 2009-2025
abstract: We tested whether total phosphorus concentration changed at fixed measured sediment, flow and season at two related Gulf river outlets. We reused USGS version 3.0 Sample extracts and compared water years 1981-1996 with 2009-2025. Separate weighted fits used a common range of flow and sediment. The retained sample had 82 early and 329 late site-dates. The equal-outlet geometric concentration factor was 1.623, with a conditional 95% three-year block bootstrap interval of 1.456 to 1.868. Both outlets and all planned checks retained a rise. Linear terms gave 1.654, no range trim gave 1.540, and positive total phosphorus minus orthophosphate gave 2.145. Thus the tested flow, sediment and season terms did not account for the era difference. This extends prior modelled load-ratio and sediment-surrogate tests with a direct conditional sample contrast. It is not independent source confirmation or a test of particle composition. Sparse early samples, missing years, assay history, selection and common-slope assumptions limit inference. The package includes code, permitted numerical extracts, provenance, aggregate results, bootstrap draws and a figure.

display.caption: Late-to-early conditional concentration factors. Lines show conditional 95% three-year block bootstrap intervals. The branches share upstream water.
